slides.headline: Light now needs 24 hours to reach Voyager 1
slides.subline: **It is 16.1 billion miles from Earth.** No human-made object has ever been this far away.

slides.body: On Nov. 18, Voyager 1 reached **one light-day** from Earth: about **16.1 billion miles**. Light travels 186,000 miles every second. [[Even at that speed]], it takes a full day to get there.
Mission teams send a command today, and Voyager gets it **tomorrow**. Its reply takes another day to come back. That is a [[two-day wait]] for a single message.

Voyager 1 launched in **1977** and still sends data from interstellar space. Its twin, Voyager 2, will not reach one light-day until [[November 2035]]. Will it still be working by then? Tell us below.
